help:metadata.help:title: Ordoprep 0.9.9.8: Complete Command and Workflow Help
help:metadata.help:subtitle: Compact, normalize, filter, partition, and connectivity-check PGN results for Ordo and other rating tools
help:metadata.help:abstract: Ordoprep reads one or more PGN streams, extracts the White, Black, and Result tags, optionally canonicalizes participant names and selects games, and writes a minimal result-only PGN. It can also remove statistically problematic participants and analyze the result graph as rating-connected groups. This manual documents the exact behavior of the local Windows executable and its matching upstream source tag.
help:metadata.help:document-status: Verified against the local executable and matching upstream source.

help:topic.help:title: Quick start
help:topic.help:purpose: Produce a small, clean PGN containing only player names and game results.

help:result.help:description: Each completed game contains only White, Black, and Result tags plus a standalone result token. Moves, comments, and every other PGN tag are omitted.

help:topic.help:title: Mental model
help:topic.help:summary: Ordoprep is an in-memory results ETL tool: it extracts PGN result records, transforms names and membership, optionally analyzes or filters those records, and emits minimal PGN or group artifacts.

help:capabilities.help:capability: Remove moves, comments, and nonessential tags while preserving game order, colors, names, and result.
Read multiple files and optionally standard input into one logical game sequence.
Replace declared aliases with a chosen canonical name before later selection and analysis.
Include or exclude games based on exact participant membership.
Remove low-performance, low-game-count, or recursively perfect-score participants.
Find independently rateable result groups, report them, split them, or retain the largest group.

help:non-goals.help:item: Ordoprep does not calculate ratings; Ordo does.
Ordoprep does not validate full PGN syntax, chess legality, or movetext.
Ordoprep does not preserve Event, Site, Date, Round, ECO, time control, opening, or provenance tags.
Ordoprep does not edit games in place; name a distinct output file.

help:syntax-notes.help:note: Use the executable name .\ordoprep-win64.exe from this workspace. Other installations may expose the command as ordoprep.
Use -- before positional PGN paths, especially if a path begins with a hyphen. Positional sources are processed after sources named by -p and -P.
Quote any path containing spaces. In PowerShell, double or single quotes are accepted by the shell.
The implementation accepts file inputs and --stdin together. Files are read first; standard input is read last.

help:input-composition.help:source-order: The single path supplied by -p, if any.
Paths read from the -P list, in list order.

help:topic.help:title: Processing pipeline and option timing
help:topic.help:summary: Ordering matters because aliases affect selection, selection affects statistics and group analysis, and group-report modes can terminate before participant filters or ordinary PGN output.

help:stages.help:stage: Parse options, reject explicit conflicts, and assemble the ordered list of input sources.
Preload canonical names and aliases from the synonym CSV.
Read each source and collect complete White/Black/Result triples in source order.
Apply either the include list or exclude list by marking nonqualifying games ignored.
Count active white wins, draws, black wins, and ignored/no-result records; print them unless quiet.
Build rating-connected groups when a group report, group split, or major-only operation was requested.
Write requested group report/player/game artifacts. Unless major-only is also active, group mode exits successfully here.
Calculate performance and apply the one selected threshold/perfect-score filter.
Write all active games, or only games wholly inside group 1 when major-only is active.
Write games marked ignored by membership or participant filtering when --remaining is present.

help:topic.help:critical-note: --groups, --group-games, or --group-players without --major-only is an analysis/splitting run, not a normal compacting run. It exits after group artifacts; an -o file may therefore be empty, and participant filters or --remaining are not reached.

help:topic.help:title: PGN input contract

help:parser-behavior.help:item: The scanner searches text lines for the exact, case-sensitive prefixes [White ", [Black ", and [Result ". Use conventional one-tag-per-line PGN.
Movetext, comments, variations, and every other tag are ignored.
A game is collected as soon as one White, one Black, and one Result value have been seen; conventional tag order is safest.
An incomplete trailing record is not emitted.
Participant matching is exact and case-sensitive unless variants are declared as aliases.
All games and names are held in memory; practical capacity is limited by available memory.

help:topic.help:warning: Any other Result-tag value terminates the run with a PGN reading error. Ordoprep reads the Result tag, not a result token appearing only in movetext.

help:rules.help:item: A path containing spaces may be enclosed in double quotes.
Each line must parse as exactly one CSV field; do not append comments or extra columns.
The first field is the output name; every later field maps to it.
Quote fields containing commas; quoting all fields is recommended.
Matching is exact and case-sensitive, so capitalization variants require explicit entries.
Avoid declaring the same alias in competing rows; the name registry is established as rows are loaded.
One exact participant name per nonblank line, optionally double-quoted.
The parser accepts one CSV field only; if a multi-column CSV is supplied, the row does not match.
Names are resolved after aliases are loaded, so either a canonical name or a declared alias can select the canonical participant.
Unmatched names warn by default but do not stop the run.

help:topic.help:title: Outputs and preservation rules

help:primary-output.help:destination: -o FILE writes to a file. Without -o, minimal PGN is written to standard output.

help:preserved.help:item: Input source order and game order.
Supported decisive/draw result, with =-= normalized to 1/2-1/2.
Participant names, after optional alias canonicalization.

help:discarded.help:item: Every tag except White, Black, and Result.
Games marked ignored by active filters.

help:topic.help:stdout-hazard: Progress, statistics, exclusion lists, and timing messages also use standard output. When the PGN itself is sent to standard output, use --quiet and do not use --timelog, or diagnostic text will contaminate the PGN stream. Using -o FILE keeps the PGN file separate from console progress.
help:topic.help:remaining-semantics: --remaining is not a universal complement of primary output. It writes decisive/drawn games explicitly marked ignored by include/exclude or participant filtering. It does not include * records, and with major-only it does not automatically contain games outside group 1.

help:topic.help:title: Participant-level filters
help:topic.help:scoring: Performance is score divided by games: win = 1, draw = 0.5, loss = 0. When a participant is removed, every game involving that participant is removed.

help:filter-semantics.help:filter: Remove participants whose current active score is either 0% or 100%, then recalculate and repeat until no further participant becomes perfect.
Calculate once and remove participants strictly below the requested percentage. A participant exactly at the threshold remains.
Calculate once and remove participants with strictly fewer than the requested number of active games. A participant exactly at the threshold remains.

help:topic.help:title: Rating connectivity and groups
help:topic.help:definition: A group is a set of participants whose results provide sufficient two-way information, directly or through cycles, to place them on one relative rating scale. Ordoprep aggregates games by ordered White/Black pairing. An aggregate containing a draw or results in both directions creates a direct two-way connection. A one-sided sweep creates only a winner-to-loser link; directed cycles can still join components.
help:topic.help:why-it-matters: Disconnected or only one-way-linked pools do not support a single reliable finite rating scale without additional assumptions. Use group analysis before sending a heterogeneous corpus to a rating program.
help:topic.help:ordering: Groups are ordered by descending participant count. Ties are resolved alphabetically by the first participant name. Therefore group 1 is the major group used by --major-only.

help:group-artifacts.help:artifact: A text pass/fail report and participant listing.
One minimal PGN per nonsingleton group.
One one-column quoted CSV per group, including singleton groups.
One minimal PGN containing only games whose two participants are both in group 1.

help:option.help:summary: Print introductory help, examples, all switches, copyright, and exit successfully.
Print only the switch list and exit successfully.
Print program name and version, then exit successfully.
Print version and GPL license notice, then exit successfully.
Suppress routine progress, statistics, uploaded-name notices, and participant exclusion listings.
help:option.help:detail: Errors remain on standard error. Unmatched include/exclude warnings require --no-warnings.

help:recommended-with.rationale: Use whenever standard output must remain clean PGN.

help:option.help:summary: Exact alias of --quiet.
Print elapsed CPU time after internal processing steps.
help:option.help:detail: Timing lines go to standard output and are not suppressed by --quiet.

help:avoid-with.condition: When -o is omitted and standard output is intended to be PGN.

help:option.help:summary: Suppress only the warnings for include/exclude list entries that match no known name.
help:option.help:detail: It does not suppress parsing, file, memory, or parameter errors.

help:option.help:summary: Add one primary PGN file.
help:option.help:detail: If repeated, only the last -p value is retained. Use positional files or -P for multiple sources.

help:option.help:summary: Read an ordered list of PGN paths from a text/one-field-CSV file.
help:option.help:detail: If repeated, only the last -P value is retained.

help:option.help:summary: Add any number of positional PGN inputs.
help:option.help:detail: The explicit -- delimiter is recommended and is required to stop option interpretation reliably.

help:option.help:summary: Read an additional PGN stream from standard input after all file inputs.
help:option.help:detail: Use --quiet when the result is also written to standard output.

help:option.help:summary: Load a CSV mapping canonical participant names to aliases.
help:option.help:detail: Aliases affect emitted names, include/exclude matching, performance aggregation, and connectivity.

help:option.help:summary: Long-form alias of --synonyms.
Keep a game only when both participants occur in the supplied name list.
help:option.help:detail: A game with one listed and one unlisted participant is excluded.

help:option.help:summary: Remove every game in which either participant occurs in the supplied name list.
Write decisive/drawn games marked ignored by membership or participant filtering.
help:option.help:detail: Not a general complement: it omits * records and does not capture the non-major groups selected away by --major-only.

help:see-also.refs: output-contract opt-include opt-exclude opt-no-perfects opt-min-perf opt-min-games

help:option.help:summary: Recursively remove participants with no wins/points or no losses/dropped points.
help:option.help:detail: After each removal wave, performance is recomputed until stable.

help:option.help:summary: Remove participants whose one-pass score percentage is strictly less than NUM.
help:option.help:detail: The parser accepts a floating-point number and does not enforce the recommended 0-to-100 range.

help:option.help:summary: Remove participants whose one-pass active game count is strictly less than NUM.
help:option.help:detail: Use uppercase -M. The upstream v0.9.9.8 README's example says -g20, but -g is actually the groups-report option in this binary.

help:option.help:summary: Write the primary minimal PGN to FILE instead of standard output.
help:option.help:detail: Choose a path distinct from every input and ensure its directory is writable.

help:option.help:summary: Write only games whose two participants belong to the largest rating-connected group.
help:option.help:detail: Group 1 is largest by participant count. Games outside it are not marked for --remaining.

help:option.help:summary: Write a text report stating whether all active participants form one rating-connected group.
help:option.help:detail: On failure, groups and their alphabetically sorted participants are listed. This mode exits after group artifacts.

help:option.help:summary: Write each nonsingleton connectivity group's games to BASE.#########.pgn.
help:option.help:detail: Group numbers are nine-digit, one-based, and ordered largest first. Singleton groups have no PGN file.

help:option.help:summary: Write each connectivity group's participant names to BASE.#########.csv.
help:option.help:detail: Each row is one double-quoted name; singleton groups are included.

help:option.help:summary: Limit the number of numbered group game/player files written.
help:option.help:detail: It does not change group analysis, --groups report content, or --major-only selection.

help:rule.help:description: Choose include or exclude, never both in one invocation.
help:rule.help:error-text: Switches -x and -i cannot be used at the same time

help:rule.help:description: At most one of --major-only, --groups/-g, --no-perfects/-d, --min-perf/-m, and --min-games/-M may be used.
help:rule.help:rationale: Each is a distinct structural selection mode in this version.
help:rule.help:error-text: Switches --major-only, -g, -d, -m, and -M cannot be used at the same time

help:rule.help:description: Any group-report/split option causes a successful early exit after group artifacts unless --major-only is also present.
help:rule.help:consequence: Without --major-only, ordinary -o output, participant filtering, and --remaining are not performed. Run connectivity diagnosis and filtering as separate commands.

help:rule.help:description: Do not combine group splitting with a participant filter.
help:rule.help:rationale: The command line is accepted, but early group-mode exit occurs before the participant filter.

help:rule.help:description: If primary PGN goes to standard output, enable quiet/silent and disable timelog.
--remaining contains explicitly ignored decisive/drawn games, not every record absent from primary output.

help:workflow.help:title: Compact one PGN
help:workflow.help:outcome: Result-only PGN in input order, with console progress kept separate.

help:workflow.help:title: Merge several PGNs
help:workflow.help:outcome: All sources become one output stream in the documented source order.

help:workflow.help:title: Canonicalize participant names
help:workflow.help:precondition: Create aliases.csv using the alias format.
help:workflow.help:outcome: Aliases are merged before selection, statistics, filtering, grouping, and output.

help:workflow.help:title: Keep a closed participant pool and audit removed games
help:workflow.help:outcome: included.pgn contains games with both players listed; excluded.pgn contains decisive/drawn games rejected by that rule.

help:workflow.help:title: Recursively remove perfect-score participants
help:workflow.help:outcome: stable.pgn contains the fixed point after recursive removal; removed.pgn records filtered games.

help:workflow.help:title: Apply minimum games or minimum performance
help:workflow.help:step: If a performance threshold is also wanted, run it as a second invocation because -M and -m conflict. .\ordoprep-win64.exe -p at-least-20.pgn -m 5 -o at-least-20-and-5pct.pgn

help:workflow.help:title: Diagnose connectivity, then extract the major group
help:workflow.help:step: Produce the report. This is intentionally a report-only invocation. .\ordoprep-win64.exe -p prepared.pgn -g groups.txt
If the report fails, extract group 1 in a separate invocation. .\ordoprep-win64.exe -p prepared.pgn --major-only -o major.pgn
help:workflow.help:outcome: major.pgn is suitable for a single connected rating calculation.

help:workflow.help:title: Split every connectivity group into games and player lists
help:workflow.help:outcome: Numbered .pgn and .csv artifacts are written; no ordinary -o output is produced.
help:workflow.help:precondition: The destination directory must already exist.

help:workflow.help:title: Use a clean standard-input/standard-output pipeline
help:workflow.help:warning: Do not add --timelog; it writes timing lines to the same standard-output stream.

help:workflow.help:title: Prepare a PGN and calculate ratings with Ordo
help:workflow.help:note: The Ordo executable name and rating options vary by installation; consult Ordo's own manual.

help:topic.help:title: Automation, streams, and exit status

help:exit-status.help:status: Includes help/version/license exits and successful group-analysis-only exits.
Used for invalid options, incompatible switches, unreadable inputs, malformed recognized tags/results, empty usable input, output failures, limits, or memory failures.

help:automation-guidance.help:item: Write PGN with -o and capture console logs separately for predictable automation.
Create parent directories before invoking group split options.
Do not assume an existing output is current merely because the process started; verify exit status and output size.
For reproducibility, record executable version, SHA-256, command line, aliases, name lists, and ordered input manifest.

help:problem.help:cause: No -p, -P, positional path, or --stdin source was recognized.
help:problem.help:resolution: Supply at least one source; use -- before positional paths.

help:problem.symptom: Problems reading results from pgn file
help:problem.help:cause: An input path could not be opened or PGN scanning failed.
help:problem.help:resolution: Check path spelling, quoting, permissions, and the first preceding parser message.

help:problem.symptom: ERROR: Input file contains no games
help:problem.help:cause: No complete, recognized White/Black/Result triple was collected, or selection left no active game.
help:problem.help:resolution: Verify exact tag capitalization, conventional tag lines, supported Result values, and include/exclude membership.

help:problem.symptom: PGN reading problems in Result tag
help:problem.help:cause: The Result tag is not one of 1-0, 0-1, 1/2-1/2, =-=, or *.
help:problem.help:resolution: Normalize malformed/alternative result strings in the source PGN.

help:problem.help:cause: A recognized White, Black, or Result prefix lacked a closing quote-and-bracket sequence.
help:problem.help:resolution: Inspect the reported line for truncated or malformed PGN tag syntax.

help:problem.help:cause: A participant-list entry did not exactly resolve to a loaded canonical name or alias.
help:problem.help:resolution: Correct case/spacing or add an alias. Use --no-warnings only after confirming unmatched names are intentional.

help:problem.symptom: Output PGN contains progress text or timing lines
help:problem.help:cause: Primary PGN and diagnostics were both written to standard output.
help:problem.help:resolution: Prefer -o FILE. Otherwise add --quiet and remove --timelog.

help:problem.symptom: The -o file is empty after a successful group command
help:problem.help:cause: Group report/split mode exits before ordinary PGN output unless --major-only is active.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use the group artifact as the intended result, or run a second command for compact/major output.

help:problem.symptom: A participant filter had no effect during group splitting
help:problem.help:cause: The accepted command exited at the group-artifact stage before reaching filtering.
help:problem.help:resolution: Filter to an intermediate PGN first, then run group splitting on that PGN.

help:problem.help:cause: The active result graph contains more than one independently rateable component or only one-way interfaces.
help:problem.help:resolution: Inspect the report, extract --major-only, or add legitimate cross-group games; do not invent results merely to connect groups.

help:problem.symptom: No games in the group, file not saved
help:problem.help:cause: The group has fewer than two participants, so it has no within-group game PGN.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use --group-players to retain a list of singleton groups.

help:problem.help:cause: The number of groups reached --group-max, default 1000.
help:problem.help:resolution: Increase --group-max if the additional artifacts are genuinely needed.

help:problem.symptom: -g 20 writes/tries to write a group report instead of filtering 20 games
help:problem.help:cause: The upstream README contains an obsolete example; in 0.9.9.8, -g requires a group-report filename and -M is minimum games.

help:term.help:name: PGN
help:term.help:definition: Portable Game Notation. Ordoprep consumes only White, Black, and Result tags from it.

help:term.help:name: canonical name
help:term.help:definition: The first field of an alias row and the participant name written to output for that alias set.

help:term.help:name: performance
help:term.help:definition: A participant's points divided by active games, expressed as a percentage.

help:term.help:name: perfect score
help:term.help:definition: Either 100% (no dropped points) or 0% (no earned points) in the current active game set.

help:term.help:name: encounter
help:term.help:definition: An aggregate of games for an ordered White/Black participant pairing used by connectivity analysis.

help:term.help:name: rating-connected group
help:term.help:definition: A component whose participants have sufficient two-way result connectivity to share a relative rating scale.

help:term.help:name: major group
help:term.help:definition: Group 1: the connectivity group with the greatest number of participants, with deterministic alphabetical tie-breaking.

help:term.help:name: remaining games
help:term.help:definition: Decisive/drawn games explicitly marked ignored by membership or participant filtering, not a universal set complement.

help:term.help:name: Ordo
help:term.help:definition: The separate rating-calculation program for which Ordoprep commonly prepares compact, connected PGN input.
